evidence: the decode intensity is (164·b)/(140 + 24·b) FLOP/byte — (164 GFLOP × b) ÷ (140 GB + 24 GB × b) for batch b, where 164 = 140 linear + 24 attention — which saturates at ~6.8 FLOP/byte as b→∞
issue: The stated saturation value is wrong: 164 ÷ 24 ≈ 6.83, but the formula as written (164·b)/(140 + 24·b) has limit 164/24 ≈ 6.83 FLOP/byte only if the numerator's coefficient is 164 and the denominator's b-coefficient is 24 — however the expression is dimensionally inconsistent (FLOP per batch element mixed with GB), and the stated KV figure of ~24 GB per sequence is wrong for the canonical case because KV at 9.2K in FP16 is ~24.1 GB per sequence but the decode KV read is per-token-step over the whole prefix, making the numerator's KV-flops term (24 GFLOP/token) inconsistent with the ~24 GB KV-read denominator at batch 1; the ratio only coincidentally lands near 6.8.
fix_instruction: State the decode intensity derivation explicitly and consistently: with per-token FLOPs F=164 GFLOP and per-sequence bytes B=140 GB (weights) + 24.1 GB (KV re-read), intensity(b) = (F·b)/(140 + 24.1·b) GB-scale, limit = F/24.1 ≈ 6.8 FLOP/byte, and label it a weight+KV-traffic upper bound; do not mix GFLOP/GB units without stating the normalization.

fix_instruction: Rewrite as a clean sum with consistent separators, e.g. "TTFT_e2e = retrieval + admission/queue + tokenization + transfer + prefill + first decode step", and state explicitly which terms are included in the 1.2 s canonical budget and which are outside it.

evidence: a 70B-parameter teaching model that stores 98% of parameters in MXFP4 and 2% in BF16 … needs 39.24375 GB of compact weight storage rather than 140 GB. Retaining this chapter's full-MHA, BF16 KV assumptions (80 layers, KV width 8192, 9,500 tokens per sequence) leaves raw KV at 24.90368 GB per sequence. In a 640 GB aggregate pool with a fixed 64 GB reserve, the storage-only integer ceiling rises from 17 sequences to 21
issue: The KV budget after weight compression should be 640 − 39.24375 − 64 ≈ 536.76 GB, giving 536.76 ÷ 24.90368 ≈ 21.5 (floor 21), but the text jumps from the raw KV figure to the ceiling "21" without showing the intermediate budget; and elsewhere (Ch. 7 §7.1 and Fig. 7.7) the concurrency ceiling of 17.5/17 is tied to the 436 GB budget, so a reader cannot verify why the reserve stays "fixed at 64 GB" when the weight footprint dropped by ~100 GB — the text leaves the reserve assumption unexplained and unstated as a limitation.
fix_instruction: Show the arithmetic explicitly (640 − 39.24375 − 64 = 536.76 GB KV budget; 536.76 ÷ 24.90368 = 21.55 → floor 21) and state that the 64 GB runtime reserve is held constant as an explicit assumption, noting that per-rank fit and fragmentation were not validated.

evidence: the population p99 of the stated 99 % log-normal + 1 % straggler mixture is 5.0 s (one extra straggler, 101 of 10,000, moves the sample p99 to 5.0 s too)
issue: The parenthetical is internally inconsistent: it states the population p99 is 5.0 s, but then says 101 stragglers out of 10,000 "moves the sample p99 to 5.0 s too" — with N=10,000 the 99th percentile rank is 9,900, so 101 stragglers would leave the sample p99 interpolated near the boundary rather than exactly at 5.0 s; the claim is presented as a fact about sampling behaviour without an explicit [ILLUSTRATIVE] tag in that sentence.
fix_instruction: Restate the sampling statement precisely (e.g. "with 100 stragglers the sorted-sample p99 interpolates at 1.33 s; with 101 stragglers the rank-9,900 draw is itself a straggler, so the sample p99 becomes 5.0 s") and tag the mixture assumption as [ILLUSTRATIVE].

fix_instruction: Replace "prefill-dominated" with an explicit qualifier (e.g. "prefill-FLOP- and KV-capacity-dominated, but decode-latency-dominated") and add a one-line note that the three senses (FLOP share, capacity pressure, wall-clock share) are distinct quantities.
